notes:
I've written verse-by-verse notes on Matthew 24:27–51 below, but several parts of your request aren't covered. I couldn't find usable material on:

- **Lutheran and Anglican readings.** No Lutheran or Anglican commentary came up. The only Methodist source is Wesley.
- **Modern scholarship.** Nothing from netbible.org or bibleodyssey.org.
- **Catholic sites.** Beyond Chrysostom's homily, nothing from catholic.com.
- **Popular modern teaching.** Nothing on prosperity, word of faith or hyper-grace readings of this passage.
- **Verse coverage.** The Enduring Word page was cut off before it reached these verses. My notes from it come from search excerpts that cover vv. 27–44 only, so for vv. 45–51 the notes rely almost entirely on Wesley.

The big split runs through the whole passage, so it comes first.

**The main dispute: is this about AD 70, the future, or both?**
- **Reformed (partial preterist):** A Ligonier devotional argues that vv. 1–35 were fulfilled when Jerusalem fell in AD 70. Otherwise, it says, Jesus' reliability is in question, because "this generation" died without seeing his final return. https://www.ligonier.org/learn/devotionals/vindication-christ
- R. C. Sproul held that the whole discourse was fulfilled between Jesus' words and AD 70. He still believed in a literal second coming, future resurrection and final judgment, based on other New Testament texts. https://www.preceptaustin.org/matthew_2434_commentary
- **Futurist (Enduring Word, Pastor David Guzik):** He reads the chapter as mostly still future. The temple's literal destruction in AD 70 sets the expectation that the rest will also be fulfilled literally. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/matthew-24/
- Elsewhere Guzik says AD 70 was a partial fulfilment and foreshadowing, with a greater fulfilment still to come. https://enduringword.com/blog-archive/qa-transcripts/correcting-my-mistakes-qa-for-january-6-2022/
- **The Gospel Coalition (middle position):** "All these things" may mean Jerusalem's fall but not Christ's return. Or AD 70 may be a first fulfilment that looks ahead to the final judgment. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/essay/preterism-prophecy-fulfilled/
- **Wesley (Methodist):** He splits the passage. Verse 29 is where Jesus "begins to speak of his last coming," and v. 34 refers to Jerusalem's fall. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/matthew/24.htm

---

**v. 27**
- Enduring Word: Christ's coming will be sudden, startling, visible everywhere, and terrifying to the ungodly. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/matthew-24/
- Wesley: the next coming will be as quick as lightning, so there will be no time for advance warnings. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/matthew/24.htm
- Chrysostom: Antichrist comes "in a place," but Christ's coming needs no herald. It shows itself instantly to the whole world. https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/200176.htm

**v. 28**
- Enduring Word: a hard saying. Probably a figure of speech meaning "when judgment is ripe, it will surely come." https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/matthew-24/
- **Older AD 70 reading:**
  - Wesley, Barnes and Clarke: the carcass is the doomed Jewish nation or Jerusalem, and the eagles are the Roman armies. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/matthew/24.htm; https://www.studylight.org/commentary/matthew/24-28.html
  - Gill (Baptist) says the eagles are not the saints but the Roman legions, whose standards bore eagles. https://www.studylight.org/bible/eng/asv/matthew/24-28.html
- **Rejections of that reading:**
  - Ellicott calls the Roman reading too narrow. He calls the Fathers' view (carcass = Christ, eagles = saints) "revolting and irrational." https://biblehub.com/commentaries/matthew/24-28.htm
  - The Pulpit Commentary says neither the Jerusalem reading nor a purely spiritual one fits the second-coming context. Its own view: as vultures at once notice a carcass, all people will at once see Christ's coming. https://biblehub.com/matthew/24-28.htm
- **Futurist judgment reading:** Thomas Ice says the image pictures judgment on unbelievers, not the events of AD 70. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/ice_thomas/Mat24-25/Mat24-25_Part20.cfm
- **Orthodox / patristic:**
  - Chrysostom says the eagles are the angels, martyrs and saints. https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/200176.htm
  - Elsewhere he reads the carcass as Christ's body in death, gathered around by believers at the Lord's Table. The editor notes that several Fathers shared this reading. https://www.ccel.org/ccel/schaff/npnf112.iv.xxv.html
- **Geneva Bible (Reformed):** the carcass is Christ, to whom all will flock like eagles. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/matthew/24-28.htm

**v. 29**
- Wesley: here Jesus turns to his last coming. "Immediately" is spoken from God's view of time, where a thousand years is as a day. Early Christians who missed this wrongly expected an instant return. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/matthew/24.htm
- Enduring Word places the cosmic signs right after the future great tribulation. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/matthew-24/

**v. 30**
- **What is "the sign"?**
  - Enduring Word: hard to say. More likely a description of Jesus' visible return than a cross in the sky. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/matthew-24/
  - MacArthur (via Precept Austin): the sign is the Son of Man himself appearing in the sky. https://www.preceptaustin.org/matthew_2430_commentary
  - Wesley: perhaps the cross. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/matthew/24.htm
- **Orthodox / patristic:**
  - Chrysostom: the sign is the cross, shining brighter than the darkened sun. Christ brings it so that those who rejected him are convicted, and they mourn when they see "that this is He." https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/200176.htm
  - An OCA reflection notes that many Fathers, Chrysostom included, read the sign as the cross. https://www.oca.org/reflections/fr.-steven-kostoff/before-thy-cross-we-bow-down-in-worship
- **Matthew Henry:** sooner or later all sinners will mourn. Repentant sinners mourn in a godly way; the unrepentant mourn in despair. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/matthew/24-40.htm
- **Reformed preterist:** the "coming on the clouds" means Christ executing judgment on that generation of unbelieving Israel. https://www.ligonier.org/learn/devotionals/vindication-christ

**v. 31**
- Wesley: "the elect" are all who have endured to the end in faith that works by love. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/matthew/24.htm
- Matthew Henry: the elect are scattered through every nation, and on the gathering day not one will be missing. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/matthew/24-40.htm
- Dispensational: those saved during the tribulation are gathered by the angels. https://www.gotquestions.org/Olivet-discourse.html

**vv. 32–33**
- Enduring Word: when the signs appear (the "abomination," then the tribulation, then the heavenly signs), the return will follow. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/matthew-24/
- **Is the fig tree Israel?**
  - Guzik rejects the popular view that the fig tree is Israel and that the generation that saw Israel's 1948 founding will see the end. "All these things" means everything Jesus listed. https://enduringword.com/who-or-what-is-the-generation-that-shall-not-pass-away-live-qa-on-may-16-2024-2/
  - Precept Austin likewise says the fig tree is a plain comparison, not a symbol of Israel. https://www.preceptaustin.org/pdf/60925/

**v. 34** (the most disputed verse)
- **Futurist:**
  - Enduring Word: it can't mean the disciples' generation, since they never saw the return of v. 30. It means the generation that sees the signs. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/matthew-24/
  - Some futurists (Bob DeWaay, quoted at length by Precept Austin) take "generation" as a moral type of people, not a time span. https://www.preceptaustin.org/matthew_2434_commentary
- **Contemporaries / AD 70:**
  - Wesley: "the generation now living." The city fell about 40 years later. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/matthew/24.htm
  - Ellicott: the natural meaning is people alive at the time. The words may mean only that the process begins. https://biblehub.com/matthew/24-34.htm
  - The Ligonier preterist case is under "The main dispute" above. https://www.ligonier.org/learn/devotionals/vindication-christ
- **Matthew Henry:** reads it as a promise that the Jews will remain a distinct people until the end. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/matthew/24-40.htm

**v. 35**
- Precept Austin: God's word outlasts the universe, so believers can trust it. https://www.preceptaustin.org/matthew-24-commentary

**v. 36**
- Enduring Word: if Jesus during his earthly ministry did not know the day, it is foolish for anyone to predict it. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/matthew-24/
- Wesley: no one knew while Jesus was on earth, though it could have been revealed to John later. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/matthew/24.htm
- Precept Austin: even during the time of signs, the exact day and hour stay unknown. https://www.preceptaustin.org/matthew-24-commentary

**vv. 37–39**
- Enduring Word: "the days of Noah" means life as usual (eating, drinking, marrying), perhaps wicked but ordinary. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/matthew-24/
- Matthew Henry: people then were careless and unbelieving. He applies this both to judgment on the Jewish nation and to the final judgment. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/matthew/24-40.htm

**vv. 40–41** (taken for rescue, or taken for judgment?)
- **Taken to Christ, the rest left:**
  - Ellicott leans this way from how the Greek word is used elsewhere. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/matthew/24-40.htm
  - Meyer agrees, linking it to the angels gathering the elect in v. 31. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/matthew/24-40.htm
  - Matthew Henry: the chosen are taken to meet the Lord; the rest are left to perish. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/matthew/24-40.html
  - Pre-tribulation rapture reading: believers removed before the tribulation. https://biblehub.com/q/Meaning_of_Matthew_24_40_on_rapture.htm
- **Taken in judgment, the righteous left:**
  - Dispensational writers Ice, Constable and Criswell (a Baptist pastor), plus Blomberg: the context is the second coming, not the rapture. Those taken are judged, as the flood "took them all away." https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/ice_thomas/Mat24-25/Mat24-25_Part34.cfm; https://www.preceptaustin.org/matthew_2437-42_commentary
  - Barnes: probably taken by death. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/matthew/24-40.htm
- **AD 70 readings:**
  - Gill (Baptist): taken by the Roman army. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/matthew/24-40.htm
  - Wesley: taken into God's protection, while the other shares the common disaster. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/matthew/24.htm
- **Undecided:** Bob Utley at bible.org says there is no secret rapture here, and it is unclear which group is blessed. https://bible.org/book/export/html/21290

**vv. 42–44**
- Enduring Word: we must be ready, because his coming is without warning. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/matthew-24/
- Wesley on v. 42: the Lord may come either to call your soul at death or to judge the nation. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/matthew/24.htm

**v. 45**
- Wesley: "wise" means always remembering that everything you have is only entrusted to you as a steward. "Faithful" means living by that conviction. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/matthew/24.htm
- Meyer links the faithful servant back to those "taken" in v. 40. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/matthew/24-40.htm

**vv. 46–47:** Nothing specific found.

**v. 48**
- Wesley: the servant has become evil by throwing off faith and a good conscience. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/matthew/24.htm
- Guzik's application: avoid the spiritual laziness of thinking Jesus' coming is delayed. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/matthew-24/

**vv. 49–50:** Nothing specific found.

**v. 51**
- Wesley: "the hypocrites" are the worst of sinners. If ministers are mainly in view, no hypocrisy is worse than claiming to serve Christ while serving greed, ambition or pleasure. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/matthew/24.htm
